topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and frames the fundamental clinical and biological themes to be covered.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concept that cancer arises from genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal differentiation, tissue architecture, and cellular growth controls.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and progression to malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained benign growths to invasive and metastatic malignancies, using clinical and histological evidence.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification rules
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the standardized naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors based on tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It details the physiological and anatomical mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors impair normal organ function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare cancer incidence patterns across human populations and diverse animal species as a shared consequence of multicellular development.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale, histological criteria, and clinical efficacy of screening programs for various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing administrative remarks, summarises the learning objectives, and previews the upcoming practical sessions.
